statement: Load a named industrial robot cell from an installed library and place its base in the model at a chosen plane.
superiority: Native robot library browser with preview and offline cache, so no internet fetch or XML copy is needed at open time.

acceptance.corpus: Library of 10 arm models (ABB, KUKA, UR, Staubli) loaded with random base planes
acceptance.tolerance: Base pose reproduced to 1e-6 mm; joint-limit data equals vendor datasheet

statement: Define a custom robot arm from Denavit-Hartenberg distances, joint ranges and speeds plus per-link display and collision meshes.

source.ref: Custom robot library (XML kinematics + layered meshes)

superiority: Validate the kinematic chain on import and flag mesh/axis mismatches with a visual diff instead of failing silently.

acceptance.corpus: Hand-built 6R arm with DH table versus vendor FK for 100 random joint sets
acceptance.tolerance: TCP position error <= 0.01 mm and orientation <= 0.001 deg vs reference FK

statement: Create an end-effector tool with TCP plane, mass, centre of mass and meshes, optionally calibrating the TCP from four flange orientations.
superiority: Report calibration residual and refuse degenerate pose sets, which the plugin leaves to the user.

acceptance.corpus: Synthetic 4-pose calibration with known TCP offset (0,0,200 mm) and 0.05 mm pose noise
acceptance.tolerance: Recovered TCP within 0.1 mm of truth; singular pose sets rejected

statement: Define a work frame that targets are measured against, fixed in space or coupled to a moving positioner or external mechanism.
superiority: Show frame hierarchy and coupling live in the viewport and recompute downstream targets when the mechanism pose changes.

acceptance.corpus: Frame coupled to a turntable rotated 0-360 deg; target world position checked at 10 angles
acceptance.tolerance: World TCP position error <= 0.01 mm at every angle

statement: Create Cartesian or joint-space targets carrying tool, frame, speed, zone, command and motion type, with values inherited from a reference target.
superiority: Typed target objects with inspector and undo, so editing one attribute never silently resets others.

acceptance.corpus: 100-target toolpath with inheritance overrides; compare attributes to expected table
acceptance.tolerance: All attributes match expected values; zero unintended overrides

statement: Solve inverse and forward kinematics for targets without building a program, choosing among multiple joint solutions by proximity to previous joints.
superiority: Return all valid IK branches with configuration flags and a continuity-aware picker, deterministic across runs.

acceptance.corpus: FK-IK-FK round trip on 10,000 random reachable poses for a 6R spherical-wrist arm
acceptance.tolerance: Round-trip pose error <= 1e-6 mm / 1e-6 rad; same branch chosen on repeat runs

statement: Define reusable speed objects with translation, rotation, external-axis speed, acceleration and optional duration limits.
superiority: Show per-segment speed profile graph and warn when a limit exceeds the controller capability.

acceptance.corpus: Toolpath with three speed objects; duration compared with hand calculation
acceptance.tolerance: Segment times within 1% of analytic distance/speed

statement: Assign approximation zones so targets are either exact stop points or blended fly-by points, and preview the blended path.
superiority: Draw the true blended corner path using the controller's published blend rules per brand.

acceptance.corpus: Right-angle corner with 10 mm and 50 mm zones; blend radius measured
acceptance.tolerance: Blend start/end distance equals the zone value within 0.5 mm

statement: Attach commands such as digital and analog outputs, waits, pendant messages and program stops to targets or the program start.

source.ref: Set DO / Set AO / Wait DI / Wait / Message / Stop Program

superiority: Validate commands against each controller's capabilities at authoring time and show them on the timeline.

acceptance.corpus: Program with 12 mixed commands exported to ABB, KUKA and UR
acceptance.tolerance: All commands emitted in source order; unsupported ones raise errors

statement: Insert manufacturer-specific code lines per brand or replace generated code entirely, with a clear note that simulation is unavailable for custom code.
superiority: Syntax-check custom lines per controller language and keep the rest of the program simulatable.

acceptance.corpus: Custom RAPID and KRL snippets injected between targets
acceptance.tolerance: Snippets appear verbatim at the correct position; syntax errors flagged

statement: Check a robot system and toolpaths for errors and warnings (reach, limits, unsupported commands) and generate controller code only when valid.
superiority: Itemize every violation with the target index, a zoomable marker and suggested fix.

acceptance.corpus: Toolpath with 20 deliberately unreachable and over-limit targets plus 100 valid
acceptance.tolerance: All 20 faults reported with correct indices; zero false positives on valid targets

statement: Generate native program code for ABB RAPID, KUKA KRL, Universal Robots, Staubli VAL3, Franka, Doosan, Fanuc, Igus and Jaka from one toolpath.
superiority: Round-trip tests per controller language against vendor simulators so output is verified, not just emitted.

acceptance.corpus: Same 50-target toolpath generated for 9 brands, parsed by each vendor's offline checker
acceptance.tolerance: Zero syntax errors; positions in output equal source targets within 0.001 mm

statement: Animate a checked program through the solved kinematics with a normalized 0-to-1 time control and posed robot meshes.
superiority: GPU-instanced rendering with scrubbing at frame rate even for multi-robot cells with large meshes.

acceptance.corpus: 6-robot cell with 5 M triangles scrubbed through a 10,000-target program
acceptance.tolerance: Median frame time <= 16 ms while scrubbing; pose equals FK at sampled times

statement: Estimate program duration from velocity limits, stop points, waits and singularity slowdowns, warning when acceleration may make it optimistic.
superiority: Integrate acceleration and jerk profiles so the estimate tracks controller execution time closely.

acceptance.corpus: Straight 1 m line at 500 mm/s with trapezoid acceleration 2 m/s2 and a corner stop
acceptance.tolerance: Estimated time within 2% of analytic trapezoid value

statement: Test posed robot, tool and environment meshes for collisions along the program, with a movable environment such as a positioner.
superiority: Continuous (swept) checking on BVH-accelerated meshes instead of sampled steps, so thin or fast intrusions are not missed.

acceptance.corpus: Synthetic 2 mm obstacle passed at 1 m/s versus sampled-step baseline
acceptance.tolerance: 100% of seeded collisions found; no false positives within 0.5 mm clearance

statement: Save generated code to a folder or upload, start and pause it on supported controllers over the network, with logged status.
superiority: Pre-flight checklist and diff of what changed since the last verified save, and no passwords stored in the file.

acceptance.corpus: Mock ABB, UR and Franka controllers receiving a 200-line program
acceptance.tolerance: Uploaded bytes equal saved file hash; run/pause commands acknowledged

statement: Model positioners, linear tracks and custom mechanisms as mechanical groups whose axis values are carried by every target.
superiority: Automatic axis-value solve that honours limits and keeps TCP world pose, versus manual per-target entry.

acceptance.corpus: Robot on 3 m track plus 2-axis positioner holding a part, 50 targets
acceptance.tolerance: World TCP error <= 0.05 mm and axis values within limits for all targets

statement: Drive several robots and mechanisms in one program by giving each mechanical group its own toolpath and coupling frames between them.
superiority: Time-synchronised multi-robot timeline with inter-robot collision checks and shared wait signalling.

acceptance.corpus: Two arms handing over a part with a shared frame at 20 handover poses
acceptance.tolerance: Handover pose agreement <= 0.1 mm; zero inter-robot collisions reported falsely

statement: Convert between planes and each manufacturer's position and orientation numbers, and between vendor joint degrees and radians with sign conventions.

source.ref: Get Plane / From Plane / Degrees To Radians

superiority: Unit-aware numeric conversions with round-trip assertions shown inline.

acceptance.corpus: 1,000 random planes converted to KUKA ABC, ABB quaternion and UR rotation vector and back
acceptance.tolerance: Round-trip plane error <= 1e-9 in rotation, 1e-6 mm in position
